task.title: Compare Origin to the addressed authority on loopback binds, not to any loopback name
task.description:
Deferred minor from the adversarial review of PR #27 (WB-01KZBT0R3KS9DCFGSRP2J7C22X, branch fix/web-origin-host-guard).

internal/webui/guard.go:134: in the loopback branch, originIsBoard returns loopbackHost(host), so any loopback name or IP on the bound port counts as "the board itself". It never compares the Origin to the authority the request actually addressed. The non-loopback branch immediately below (guard.go:136) already does the right thing by comparing against requestHost.

Failure scenario: the board is on 127.0.0.1:7331. A separate local server binds [::1]:7331 — a distinct socket on the same port number — and serves a page. That page runs fetch("http://127.0.0.1:7331/api/tasks", {method:"POST", headers:{"Content-Type":"application/json"}, ...}) and sends Origin: http://[::1]:7331. The response is unreadable to the attacker page (the board sends no CORS headers), but the request still executes: a task is created and boardPublisher pushes it to origin, which is the injection path the parent ticket exists to close. Reviewer reproduced this against the extracted guard: reject(bound="127.0.0.1:7331", Host="127.0.0.1:7331", Origin="http://[::1]:7331", CT=json) returns 0 (allowed), and the same for Origin http://127.0.0.2:7331.

This is also looser than what the code and docs promise: the doc comment on GuardSameOrigin says an Origin "must name the board itself", and README.md:666 says the same.

Fix: in the loopback branch, compare the origin authority to the already-accepted request authority, as the non-loopback branch does — i.e. drop the special case and always require the origin host to equal requestHost on the bound port. This breaks nothing legitimate, because a browser's Origin always matches the authority it addressed: a page loaded from localhost:7331 sends Origin http://localhost:7331 with Host localhost:7331, and 127.0.0.1:7331 stays self-consistent the same way. Add a guard test for the mismatched-loopback-authority case.

Why deferred from PR #27: it requires another local server to already hold the same port on a different loopback address, so it is a narrower path than the cross-site case the ticket's acceptance criteria name, and all of those are met by what shipped. Tightening the branch changes the accepted-Origin contract, so it belongs in its own change with its own test rather than in a PR already under review.
